person.name: Patrick Vieira
person.headline: AI Platform Engineer
person.tagline: I build the platforms, infrastructure and identity systems that let a small team ship like a large one, and I hold the AI agents writing that team's code to the same standard as people.

about: I design the architecture and run the infrastructure, identity and security that other engineers build on, and I write the engineering standards they work to.

Much of my recent work is about making AI-assisted delivery trustworthy. Agent-written code goes through the same checks as anyone's: a written spec before code, tests first, a hook that stops an agent finishing until typecheck, lint and tests pass, and adversarial review by a model from a second vendor.
I do my best work in small teams. I set technical direction by writing architecture decision records, choose platforms on measured evidence, and automate any job nobody should be doing by hand.

work.title: Internal developer platform for AI-assisted delivery
work.summary: A Claude Code platform for a whole engineering team, built around a golden path from spec to merge. It is a plugin of 21 skills and 3 hook events for spec-first authoring, test-driven implementation and cross-vendor adversarial review, plus a versioned engineering-standards baseline pushed automatically to about 26 repositories.

work.title: Agent execution and evaluation platform
work.summary: Coding agents take specified work, build in sandboxed containers with per-run credentials, pass rubric-graded review gates and merge on automated criteria. It is still being built, on the same spec-to-merge path. I chose the platform after a spike measured a 3.3 s cold start and a 32 ms warm one.

work.title: Passkey and verifiable-credential identity
work.summary: did:web identity with WebAuthn passkeys and W3C Verifiable Credentials, built from scratch. It is in production as the sign-in for a suite of internal applications and federates to self-hosted DIDs, this domain among them.

work.title: Infrastructure as code
work.summary: Cloud and SaaS infrastructure across GitHub, Cloudflare, Kafka, Databricks and observability, run through Terraform Cloud with GitOps: plan on pull request, apply on merge, daily drift detection. AWS and Microsoft 365 are code too, and joiners and leavers are automated.

work.title: On-premises speech intelligence
work.summary: A meeting-transcription pipeline on an NVIDIA DGX Spark (NeMo ASR, diarisation and voiceprint speaker naming) for audio that cannot leave the building.

side_projects.title: Kaizen Kingdom
side_projects.summary: An adaptive maths learning platform, started after seeing in the classroom how far edtech falls short of what teachers need.

side_projects.title: Marine-weather agent
side_projects.summary: An agent that emails forecasts to a sailing yacht at sea.

background: I studied Electrical and Electronic Engineering (BEng), then trained as a maths teacher (PGCE, UCL) and taught secondary mathematics for two years. In 2021 I taught myself full-stack development and moved into software, and I have worked in platform engineering since 2023.
Two years in a classroom left me judging tooling by whether people pick it up and use it well.

faq.q: Who is Patrick Vieira, the engineer?
faq.a: Patrick Vieira is a platform engineer based in London — not the footballer of the same name. He designs and runs the foundations other engineers build on: architecture, infrastructure, identity and security.
Platform engineering, AI-assisted software delivery, infrastructure as code and passkey-based identity, mainly with TypeScript, Python, Cloudflare and Terraform.

An internal developer platform for AI-assisted delivery, an agent execution and evaluation platform, a passkey and verifiable-credential identity system, infrastructure as code across cloud and SaaS, and an on-premises speech pipeline.

faq.q: How does he make AI-written code trustworthy?
faq.a: He holds it to the same bar as anyone's code. A spec comes before any code and tests come first; a hook won't let an agent finish until typecheck, lint and tests pass; and a model from a second vendor reviews the change.
